text:
The Jets fell behind by two goals in Dallas, then scored eight of the next nine, and the win stretched their streak to five straight. Mark Scheifele, picked seventh overall by Winnipeg in 2011 out of Barrie, scored twice and added an assist. Dawson Mercer also scored twice, including a backhand with nine seconds left in the second period that made it 5-3. Kyle Connor had a goal and two assists.

The first period belonged to Dallas. Arttu Hyry's snap shot at 4:19 and Roope Hintz's backhand at 18:32 made it 2-0, and the two teams were close on expected goals (the quality of chances, which we measure by how likely each shot was to score), 1.29 for DAL to 1.22 for WPG. Winnipeg took over in the second, out-chancing Dallas 1.96 to 0.73. Dylan Samberg and Scheifele tied the game, David Perron's deflection briefly put Dallas back ahead, and then Mercer, Scheifele on the power play and Mercer again put the Jets up 5-3. Connor, Gabriel Vilardi and Cole Koepke scored in the third, the last two 14 seconds apart.

Dallas had more shot attempts, 65 to 54, and the Stars were the better team in the third, but the goaltending decided it. Jake Oettinger allowed six goals on 27 shots, about 2.7 more than the chances against him called for. Stuart Skinner stopped 30 of 33 for Winnipeg, a bit better than expected. Our numbers gave the Jets 55 percent of simulated replays, so the margin was far wider than the play. The Jets now have five straight wins, while Dallas, which beat Winnipeg 3-2 in overtime on Oct. 22, has to sort out its goaltending.
